title: Christian Pulisic back in training with full team ahead of USMNT’s World Cup group finale
content:
IRVINE, Calif. — Christian Pulisic participated in full U.S. men’s national team training for the 15 minutes open to the media on Monday ahead of Thursday’s World Cup group finale against Turkey. It’s a sign that the U.S. star is on his way to being fully cleared, no matter if he features in the match at SoFi Stadium or not. U.S. Soccer declined to give official word on his status beyond what was able to be witnessed on the training field at Great Park.

Pulisic, 27, missed Friday’s 2-0 win over Australia with a left calf injury. The star winger, who set up the Americans’ first two goals in their 4-1 win over Paraguay, left the game with tightness in his calf after taking a kick during the game. That compounded an issue that started with a knock he took in training earlier in the week.

After the game, Pulisic expressed optimism it wouldn’t be a bigger issue and that coming out of the game was “precautionary.”

“I’m hoping I’ll be fine the next few days,” he said.

Over the next week, Pulisic’s day-to-day status was under the microscope. The winger took part in “modified training sessions” in which he worked in the gym at the training center and individually on an adjacent practice field. Cameras tracked him running through resistance training and doing light ball work.

In the end, he was held out of the Australia game.

“Christian is not available,” Pochettino told Fox in the hours ahead of the eventual win in Seattle. “The evolution is really well. Today, he was training in the morning in the camp and I’ve seen the feelings are good. I hope as soon as possible he can be ready to be selected again and to be part of the team. … A little bit sad because he wanted to stay, he wanted to participate today.”

With the win over Australia, the U.S. will take on an already-eliminated Turkey team in a dead-rubber match that holds no implications for the tournament. The Americans will play on July 1 in the round of 32 in Santa Clara, Calif., against a third-place team from another group.

It could be a good opportunity for Pulisic to get some minutes and get back into some form ahead of the knockout stage. Two former U.S. coaches, Gregg Berhalter and Bob Bradley, suggested as such on FanDuel’s Coaches’ Corner show.

“If he’s ready to go, I would say you want to play him,” Berhalter said. “You don’t want that much time. And it may not be the whole game, but you want to give him an opportunity to play based on his health.”

Bradley agreed.

“Calf injuries are tricky,” he said. “As they are going through all the steps in the return to play, you’re going to get an indication of exactly where he is. You don’t want to rush him, that’s for sure. But when you start thinking about the Paraguay game and the number of days before you get to the round of 32, that’s a long time without playing.”

With Pulisic appearing to be back on the field this week, Pochettino can now evaluate the best way to work him into the mix and get him ready for July 1.
